ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a horizontal line extending to the right from near the label A on the left side; from A there is also drawn an oblique line slanting down to the right. In the lower left, there is an oblique side extending up to the right and passing through the horizontal line, and near the intersection point it is labeled 100°. At the lower left corner, between this oblique side and a gentler oblique line going up to the right, it is labeled 40°. At the intersection of the two diagonal lines in the middle, the upper included angle is labeled 110°. Reasoning: Take the horizontal ray from A to the right as the reference direction, and let angle A, that is, the angle between the horizontal ray and the oblique line from A down to the right, be x. The 100° marked at the left oblique side and the horizontal line is supplementary to the acute angle formed by this oblique side with the horizontal line, so the acute angle of this oblique side relative to the horizontal line is 180° - 100° = 80°, that is, it makes 80° with the horizontal line going up to the right. At the lower left corner, the angle between this oblique side and the middle oblique line going up to the right is 40°, therefore the middle oblique line going up to the right makes 80° - 40° = 40° with the horizontal line. At the central intersection point, the marked 110° is the angle between the ray going up to the right with direction 40° and the ray going up to the left along the unknown oblique line pointing toward A. If the unknown oblique line starting from A is inclined downward by x relative to the horizontal line, then the direction angle of the reverse ray pointing from the intersection point to A is 180° - x. Therefore there is (180° - x) - 40° = 110°, solving gives 140° - x = 110°, so x = 30°.

raw_record.question_text: The degree measure of angle $A$ is

method.method_draft: Label the top horizontal ray from A to the right as the reference direction, and let the desired angle at A be x, between this horizontal ray and the descending diagonal from A. From the image, read the 100° angle where the left slanted side crosses the top horizontal line; since it is supplementary to the acute angle that slanted side makes with the horizontal, the slanted side is 180° - 100° = 80° above the horizontal. At the lower-left vertex, the angle between this slanted side and the rising diagonal through the middle is 40°, so that rising diagonal is 80° - 40° = 40° above the horizontal. At the central crossing, the marked 110° is between the ray going up-right along this 40° diagonal and the ray going up-left toward A along the unknown diagonal. The direction of the ray from the crossing back to A is 180° - x, so (180° - x) - 40° = 110°. Solve to get x = 30°.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中有一条从左侧标记 A 附近向右延伸的水平线；从 A 还引出一条向右下方倾斜的斜线。左下方有一条斜边向右上方延伸并穿过水平线，交点附近标有 100°。左下角处，这条斜边与一条向右上方较平缓的斜线之间标有 40°。中间两条对角线相交处，上方夹角标有 110°。
推理：把从 A 向右的水平射线作为参考方向，设角 A，即水平射线与从 A 向右下方斜线之间的角为 x。左侧斜边与水平线处标出的 100° 与该斜边同水平线形成的锐角互补，所以该斜边相对水平线的锐角为 180° - 100° = 80°，即它向右上方与水平线成 80°。左下角处该斜边与中间向右上方斜线的夹角是 40°，因此中间向右上方斜线与水平线成 80° - 40° = 40°。在中央交点，标出的 110° 是方向为 40° 的向右上方射线和沿未知斜线指向 A 的向左上方射线之间的角。若从 A 出发的未知斜线比水平线向下倾斜 x，则从交点指向 A 的反向射线方向角为 180° - x。因此有 (180° - x) - 40° = 110°，解得 140° - x = 110°，所以 x = 30°。
